The challenge

What makes event & wedding venues different.

01

Wedding and corporate inquiries need dates, guest counts, budgets and spaces checked before a useful reply is possible.

02

Forgotten tentative holds block peak dates, and double bookings of a lawn or hall are a real risk.

03

Vendors, the client and the family coordinate through scattered WhatsApp groups, so late changes surface on the day.

04

Run sheets and function sheets are rebuilt by hand for every event.

Where automation helps

Practical uses for event & wedding venues.

01

Inquiry qualification and date checks

Event type, date flexibility, guest count, space and budget captured from any channel and checked against the venue calendar, with alternative dates offered when the first choice is taken.

02

Tentative holds with expiry

Each hold has an owner and an expiry date, reminders go to the client and the owner, and holds the owner does not extend are released on expiry so dates return to sale.

03

Package-based proposals

Proposal drafts from approved packages, menus and policies, edited and approved by the sales manager, with a payment link for the advance.

04

Vendor and client coordination

Task lists, deadlines and update links for decorators, caterers, sound and photographers, with a change log the client can see.

05

Final counts, instalments and run sheets

Instalment reminders, a final guest count locked at the agreed cut-off, and function and run sheets generated from the same event record.

06

Annual event rebooking

Alerts to the sales manager ahead of a corporate client's annual event date, and consented anniversary greetings for past wedding clients.

Quote, confirm and payAdvanced5–8 weeks

Group, MICE and wedding inquiry desk

Turn group RFPs, corporate offsites and wedding inquiries into qualified opportunities with a checked date, a tentative hold that expires on schedule, and a proposal draft built from approved packages for the sales manager to finalize.

Hotels & resorts · Event & wedding venues

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Group and event inquiries carry large revenue but need many details: dates, room blocks, function space, menus, guest counts and budgets. They arrive as PDFs, forms, calls and WhatsApp messages. Tentative holds are forgotten and block dates, proposals take days, and double bookings of a lawn or ballroom are a real risk.

Trigger

An RFP email, website event form, WhatsApp inquiry or planner lead tagged as group, corporate event or wedding.

How it runs

  • Extract event type, dates and flexibility, guest count, room block, function space, food and beverage needs and budget from the message or attached RFP using AI, flagging gaps.
  • Ask the client for missing essentials through a short form, then score fit against agreed rules such as minimum spend, peak dates and space capacity.
  • Check function space and room block availability in the banquet calendar and PMS, showing conflicts and alternative dates.
  • Place a tentative hold with an owner and expiry date, remind the client and the owner before it expires, and release the hold on expiry unless the owner extends it.
  • Draft a proposal from approved packages, menus and policies with indicative pricing for the sales manager to edit.
  • On approval, send the proposal and a payment link for the advance, and convert the hold to definite when the signed contract and advance arrive.

Human checkpoint

The sales manager approves fit, pricing, concessions and the proposal before it goes out, and the revenue manager signs off room block rates on high-demand dates. Contract and cancellation terms are confirmed by the person authorized to sign.

Prepare for arrivalStandard4–6 weeks

Event planning, vendor coordination and run sheet

Once an event is confirmed, track vendor tasks, client decisions, instalments and the final guest count against deadlines, then generate the event-day run sheet and function sheets from the same record.

Event & wedding venues

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

A wedding or conference involves decorators, caterers, sound, florists, photographers and the client's family or organizer, coordinated through scattered WhatsApp groups. Late menu decisions, changed guest counts and unconfirmed vendor timings surface on the day, and the run sheet is rebuilt by hand for every event.

Trigger

A contract marked definite in the CRM or banquet system, with the event date, package and agreed milestones.

How it runs

  • Create the event plan from a template for the event type, with milestones for menu tasting, decor sign-off, vendor confirmations, instalments and final guest count.
  • Give each vendor and the client a task list and a secure update link, and send reminders on WhatsApp or email before each deadline.
  • Collect menu choices, decor selections and changes in one place, with a change log the client can see.
  • Send instalment payment links on schedule and lock the final guest count at the agreed cut-off, alerting the event manager to late changes.
  • Generate function sheets for kitchen, banquet and housekeeping teams and a minute-by-minute run sheet with vendor arrival times, contacts and the sound cut-off time set by local rules.
  • Share the run sheet with the event team the day before and track open issues on the day in one channel.

Human checkpoint

The event manager approves the final run sheet, any change after the guest count cut-off and any vendor substitution. The venue's licensing and safety owner confirms permits such as liquor, music and fire approvals before the event.

Feedback and recoveryStandard3–5 weeks

Feedback, service recovery and review replies

Ask every guest for private feedback after a stay, meal, trip or event, open a recovery case when something went wrong, invite every guest to review without filtering, and draft replies to public reviews for a manager to approve.

Hotels & resorts · Restaurants & cloud kitchens · Travel agencies & tour operators · Event & wedding venues

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Unhappy guests often say nothing until they post a review, and happy guests rarely write one unless asked. Replies to Google, OTA and aggregator reviews are slow or generic, and some businesses ask only satisfied guests for reviews, which Google's review policies prohibit.

Trigger

Checkout in the PMS, a closed bill or delivered direct order, a trip's return date or the day after an event, plus each new public review on a connected platform.

How it runs

  • Send a short private feedback request through an approved template or email, timed for each segment; aggregator orders are left out because the platform holds that customer relationship.
  • Open a recovery case for low scores or complaint keywords, assigned to the guest relations, outlet, consultant or event manager with a response target.
  • Send every eligible guest the same review invitation regardless of their feedback score, with no incentive attached.
  • Collect new public reviews from Google Business Profile and other connected sources, and classify sentiment, topics and any serious allegation.
  • Draft a specific, courteous reply in the brand voice from the review and approved facts, and route serious allegations such as food safety, discrimination or injury to the general manager.
  • Post the approved reply through the Google Business Profile API where connected, or give the approver a copy-ready reply for the OTA or aggregator extranet.

Human checkpoint

A named manager edits and approves every public reply and decides every refund, compensation or goodwill gesture. Allegations involving safety, health, discrimination or legal threats go to the general manager or owner before any response.

Return and referStandard4–6 weeks

Repeat guest, loyalty and win-back program

Use visit and booking history to recognize regulars, send consented offers on occasions that matter to each guest, invite lapsed guests back, and remind sales ahead of corporate clients' annual events.

Restaurants & cloud kitchens · Travel agencies & tour operators · Event & wedding venues

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Most hospitality businesses hold years of guest data in POS, booking and CRM systems but rarely use it. Regulars are not recognized, birthdays and anniversaries pass unnoticed, and repeat corporate events go to competitors because nobody called in time. Mass promotions that ignore consent damage trust and break messaging rules.

Trigger

Scheduled segment updates from POS, booking and CRM data, plus date-based triggers such as birthdays, anniversaries, trip anniversaries and the anniversary of a corporate event.

How it runs

  • Build a single guest profile from POS, booking and CRM records with visit frequency, spend band, preferences and consent status per channel.
  • Define segments with the marketing owner, such as regulars, lapsed guests, occasion dates, repeat travelers by destination interest and corporate event clients.
  • Send approved marketing templates or emails only to guests with marketing opt-in, with an opt-out in every message and frequency caps.
  • Track visit-based rewards in the POS loyalty module for restaurants, suggest trips from past destinations for travel, and alert venue sales managers ahead of a client's annual event date.
  • Measure returns, bookings and opt-outs per campaign against a holdout group, and retire offers that do not bring guests back.

Human checkpoint

The marketing owner approves segments, offers and every template. The sales manager personally handles outreach to corporate and event clients. Discounts beyond agreed limits need owner approval.

Marketing consent is recorded separately from service messaging, opt-outs apply across channels promptly, and birthdays or anniversaries are collected only when the guest chooses to share them. Profiles of inactive guests are deleted after an agreed period.

What we deliver

How we measure it

  • Lapsed guests returning after a campaign
  • Opt-out rate per campaign
  • Corporate event rebookings
